standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of quasi-finiteness at a point by the existence of affine neighbourhoods in which the point is isolated in the fibre
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 3683-3687 and at the end of the proof
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the first step and the final step of the equivalence chain.

standard_prerequisites.name: Fibres of locally finite type morphisms are Jacobson schemes, cited from the same chapter with the base change statement for finite type morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that an isolated point of the fibre contains a closed point, hence is itself closed.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of locally finite type morphisms by finite type ring maps on affine charts, and the description of the fibre ring as the tensor product with the residue field, together with the algebra definition of quasi-finiteness at a prime
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the closedness and non-specialization hypothesis into the vanishing of the dimension of the fibre ring at the point, which is the algebraic quasi-finiteness condition.

core_obligations: From quasi-finiteness to isolation: quasi-finiteness at the point gives opens in which the point is isolated in the fibre, and since the fibre of the open is an open part of the whole fibre, the point is isolated in the whole fibre as well (proof lines 3683-3688).

From isolation to closedness plus absence of specializations: the fibre is a Jacobson scheme, so the singleton consisting of an isolated point contains a closed point, whence the point is closed in the fibre, and no distinct point specializes to it by openness of the singleton (proof lines 3690-3697).

From that hypothesis to the ring condition: on affine charts the coordinate ring map is of finite type, and the corresponding prime of the fibre ring is maximal with no other point of the spectrum specializing to it, whence the local ring of the fibre ring at that prime has dimension zero, which is exactly quasi-finiteness at the prime (proof lines 3699-3719).

Closing the cycle: the ring condition implies quasi-finiteness at the point by definition, and isolation of the point in the fibre implies the ring condition on any affine open containing the point (proof lines 3721-3727).
proof_roadmap: Show that quasi-finiteness at the point is equivalent to isolation in the fibre, use the Jacobson property of the fibre for closedness, and then translate the closedness and non-specialization hypothesis into the dimension-zero condition on the local ring of the fibre ring (proof lines 3683-3719).
Close the cycle by the definition of quasi-finiteness and the passage to affine opens (proof lines 3721-3727).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects four equivalent descriptions of quasi-finiteness at a point: the definition, isolation of the point in its fibre, closedness in the fibre together with the absence of distinct specializations to it, and the corresponding quasi-finiteness condition for the ring map on any affine chart through the point (statement lines 3663-3681). The counted proof is a complete chain: it passes from the definition to isolation using that the fibre of an open is open in the whole fibre, uses the Jacobson property of fibres to deduce closedness from isolation, converts the closedness and non-specialization hypothesis into the vanishing of the dimension of the local ring of the fibre ring, and closes the cycle with the definition and the passage to affine opens (proof lines 3683-3727). It is H2: every step is carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard Jacobson, finite type and fibre ring statements.
